newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW-Brazil's Acominas sees sales up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Brazil's Acominas sees sales up in 1997.

text.p: Sales by Brazilian steelmaker Acominas will dip this year due to slumping steel prices but rebound in 1997 to $700 million as prices pick up, a company official said.
Acominas President Luiz Andre Rico Vicente said in an interview that the firm expects to post sales this year totalling $650 million, down from $678 million in 1995.
Even so, Acominas' bottom line is already brighter this year, due to higher financial revenues from monetary correction, he added.
Net profit in the first eight months reached $31.5 million compared with $30 million all last year, officials said.
Rico Vicente said the firm is maintaining its plans to invest $500 million over five years to boost output up to 3.7 million tonnes.
He said production at Acominas currently stands at 2.5 million tonnes, some 25 percent over installed capacity.
The higher-than-capacity output is the result of improved production and management methods but does not jeopardize workers' safety, he added.
"We are operating with ample safety margins but have been able to gain in the process in technology and management," he said.
The steelmaker boasts the world's third-lowest operating costs, he added.

Designed by the Brazilian government in the 1970s to produce up to 10 million tonnes of steel a year, Acominas' mill is located some 62.1 miles (100 km) from Minas Gerais's state capital of Belo Horizonte.
It began producing 10 years ago, quickly amassed huge debts and was privatized in September 1993.
Its new private owners restructured the firm's debts, which had swelled to $250 million, were owed to 40 banks and bore interest rates of up to 50 percent.
"It was absurd," Rico Vicente said.
The firm has managed to restructure about $270 million in payments over five years and reduced interest rates to about nine percent, he added.
The move was part of a five-phase debt-restructing, cost-cutting and investment plan, which calls for $500 million in spending over the next five years, he said.
Under the plan, Acominas will begin producing steel blocks, reducing costs by $9 a tonne, and build a new steel furnace aimed at boosting production by a million tonnes a year, Rico Vicente said.
The firm is studying a capital increase of $150 million to $250 million to partly finance the projects, the first phase of which will cost $350 million.
"The company has to be competitive in world markets and our benchmarks are competition in Asia, the world's most competitive market," he said.
"Today, whoever does not have low production costs does not survive," he added.
-- Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
